## Immediate commands and save invariants

The two coordinator failures in `/tmp/siltwake-m1-coordinator-command-repro.json` were reproduced before fixing them.

- Taking the helm immediately copies carrier position and velocity to the player while changing ownership/mode. It no longer waits for a simulation tick to become serializable.
- A successful field repair immediately clears a recovery operation targeting that hull. Recovery updates also discard operations whose hull is missing, repaired or berthed, including a stale ready operation.
- Existing strict ownership/recovery validation remains. Interior world position must now also match the carrier-local transform within 0.01 m; walking bounds derive from the same layout descriptor.
- No save path advances time, repairs invalid ownership or bypasses validation. The existing exclusive writer, journal, session cancellation and renderer-readiness paths were not modified.

Regressions use production command/codec seams with no tick between commands and saves. They cover helm, refused leave-helm, station keeping, leave-helm, tow then repair, atomic refused repair and incapacity cancellation. A real `SiltwakeApp` composition test pauses in the carrier panel, queues a manual save behind a writer lock, blurs, attempts later controls/Resume and verifies the captured coherent snapshot commits while the app stays paused.

On the final source, the retained-save diagnostic reports valid before/after helm, **pose distance 0**, and valid before/tow/after repair with **operation null / hull enabled**. These are seeded rules diagnostics, not ordinary expedition recovery evidence.

## Exact physical contracts proposed to root

Existing public command/update/renderer signatures remain. New or extended contracts:

```ts
// src/sim/carrier.ts
export const CARRIER_LAYOUT; // authoritative readonly carrier-local metres
export function carrierRooms(
  configuration: CarrierState["configuration"],
): readonly Solid[];
export function carrierStructure(
  configuration: CarrierState["configuration"],
  transferSlot?: 0 | 1,
): Solid[];
export function carrierTransferPath(
  s: GameState, v: VehicleState, slot: 0 | 1,
  type: "launch" | "capture",
): Vec3[]; // world-space keel route; requires a present carrier

// src/sim/types.ts
interface Capsule {
  radius: number;
  height: number; // top above the pose datum
  bottom?: number; // lower offset; default 0
  halfWidth?: number; // fixed X half-extent, else radius
  halfLength?: number; // fixed Z half-extent, else radius
}

// src/sim/world.ts
export function createWorldQueries(
  solids: readonly Solid[] = SOLIDS,
  floorHeight: (x: number, z: number) => number = surfaceHeight,
): WorldQueries;
export function sweptHullClearance(
  world: WorldQueries, path: readonly Vec3[], shape: Capsule,
): boolean;

// src/content/registry.ts
export const BERTH_ENVELOPES; // aligned full rectangular hull bounds
```

`carrierStructure` returns the dry room walls/roofs/floors, deck around hatch openings, lower-lock floor, throat side shields and outer gate. Omitting `transferSlot` seals all hatches/gate; specifying a slot opens only that berth's floor hatch and the outer gate. `carrierRooms` also supplies inaccessible walking volumes, including empty sealed rooms. Walking uses these descriptors and the existing capsule; reconfiguration refuses if the replacement compartment would cover the diver. The renderer consumes the same structure and opens its selected hatch/gate only during the lock phase.

All dimensions below are **carrier-local metres, Y up, relative to the existing saved keel datum**. Min/max describe free room volumes or named structural bounds; wall material extends outward by 0.08 m.

| Element | Final bounds / position |
| --- | --- |
| Wall thickness | 0.08 |
| Deck | min `(-6.3,3.8,-12)`, max `(6.3,4,12)` |
| Port compact dry volume | min `(-6,4,-2.8)`, max `(-0.45,8.4,4.8)` |
| Starboard compact dry volume | min `(0.55,4,-2.8)`, max `(6,8.4,4.8)` |
| Medium dry volume | min `(-6,4,-3.7)`, max `(0.1,8.4,5.7)` |
| Lower lock bounds | min `(-6,-0.5,-3.7)`, max `(6,3.8,5.7)` |
| Lower lock rail keel | Y `-0.3` |
| Throat shields/gate bounds | min `(-3.1,-0.5,-12)`, max `(3.1,3.8,-3.8)` |
| Outer gate | Z `-11.5`, thickness 0.08 |
| Rail turn | `(0,-0.3,-9)` |
| Saved berths, unchanged | port `(-3,4,1)`; starboard `(3,4,1)` |
| Saved launch transform, unchanged | `(0,-3,-17)`; Spindle endpoint world Y `-0.4` |
| Helm / aft vestibule / exterior vestibule, unchanged | `(0,4,-6)` / `(4,4,9)` / `(10,3,9)` |
| Existing walking bounds, unchanged | X `[-4.7,4.7]`, Z `[-11,10]`, Y `4` |

Hearthline retains its broad radius **17**, top **9.2** and saved datum; its new lower extent is **-0.5**. Both lower-lock metal and throat/gate metal stop at that underside. The route descends through open water beyond/below the shields. An earlier A0 throat skirt reached -3.3 below the datum and escaped that proxy. A focused obstruction repro caught it. Extending the entire broad proxy to -3.3 falsely blocked the retained fixture position against terrain, so that attempt was rejected; the final minimal shell removes the protruding skirt. Neither fixture/world vessel poses nor saved transforms were moved. The underside and retained-fixture clearance regressions now both pass.

Aligned full hull envelopes, in metres from keel:

| Hull | Half width | Half length | Top height |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dart / Hush | 2.5 | 3.6 | 2.1 |
| Spindle | 2.4 | 3.7 | 1.7 |
| Creel | 2.9 | 3.3 | 3.6 |
| Mantle | 2.9 | 4.5 | 4.0 |

These describe guided, upright rail alignment. Ordinary piloting retains the broader existing proxies. The launch path is berth → same X/Z at rail Y -0.3 → centre X 0 at rail Y/Z 1 → rail turn → independent launch endpoint. Capture includes the actual independent position → endpoint and reverses the rail path.

Preflight checks the **entire envelope along every segment** before allocating a prepared transaction. Commit checks the route again against current world/terrain, carrier structure and other craft. Independent capture approach additionally uses the broad piloting proxy. Local geometry follows carrier yaw; external checks use a conservative world-axis bounding box for the rotated footprint. Solid sweeps are continuous. Terrain retains the shared 0.2 m movement slices and footprint sampling; this is not a new continuous terrain or arbitrary hull-rotation solver.

The tests exercise port/Dart, starboard/Spindle and medium/Creel launch and capture; thin blockers on every segment; clear endpoints with a blocked intervening throat; obstruction after preparation; save/reload in prepared/lock phases; interruption/rollback/retry; station keeping; other-craft obstruction; yaw; isolated hatches; dry Spindle; and exactly-once completion. Full browser feasibility for all configurations remains open. No fluid simulation, moving interior or broad visual polish was added.

## Save compatibility proposal

Retain **schema 2 / content `expedition.2`**: no persistent fields or saved berth/launch transforms changed.

Decode first performs strict shape/semantic validation. If an otherwise valid old walking pose now intersects a sealed compartment or its shell, it relocates **only the player** to the clear helm passage, resets player velocity and supplies explicit `migration`/feedback explaining the move. Fleet, cargo, discoveries and active transactions are retained. The relocation is idempotent. Loading does not write storage; the first explicit save retains the original raw generation in the existing journal backup. The new regression verifies all of these behaviors. Encoding a current pose inside a closed compartment fails rather than silently saving a relocated state.

All ten retained principal author saves decode on `558c28c`; see `/tmp/siltwake-m1-a0/retained-save-compatibility-558c28c.json`. This confirms record compatibility, not final physical clearance of old campaign Dart poses. No automatic vessel relocation is proposed. Core/fixture completion must still assess actual legacy routes under the full physical envelopes.

## Exact transient audio contract

The `GameEvent` sound variant gains **`origin?: Vec3`**, a detached **world-space position copied at emission**, never stored in `GameState` or saves. Existing cue values are unchanged. Hunter warnings and attacks provide origins. Oxygen, food, personal pressure, depleted-power and hull-pressure alarms omit them.

`Soundscape.event(e, s?)` pans only an event with an explicit origin and a listener state, using current listener position/yaw. It no longer treats the current hunter position as a fallback for every warning. Originless events stay centred. Captions/notices, activation/settings/mute/volume/disposal behavior remain unchanged.

The failing audio repro panned a low-air alarm to 0.7333 toward the hunter. The passing probe checks centred body/equipment alarms, detached threat origin after the hunter moves, and listener-yaw reversal. Actual audible mix acceptance remains open because the browser host is muted.

## Remaining obligations and handoff

The original M1-01 requirements and the Astra audit's [P0–P5 / F0–F3](M1-COORDINATION-ASTRA.md#combined-evidence-checkpoints) remain later obligations. This bounded run contributes command/fixture observations without closing those matrices:

- **P0:** final integrated New/opening/refuge, skip/replay/interruption without duplicated rewards or drain.
- **P1:** final reef-first full route and alternate island-first segment; evidence/provenance, distinct resource contexts and conservative first-access margins.
- **P2:** earned preparation/crafting/Dart launch, inventory/prerequisite/output refusals, transfer/buoy identity and personal-versus-hull protection.
- **P3:** final powered Canopy investigation, warning equivalents, counterplay/retreat/return/service and measured ≥25% first-access air/power margins.
- **P4:** gameplay-caused incapacity/disabled Dart, actual local recovery with identity/conservation, another failed rescue and continued recovery; food/power edges.
- **P5:** final return/recovery second-session saves and complete state comparison, plus command/save and lifecycle interruption evidence on assembled source.
- **F0:** production-control stationary interior/helm/vestibule and large-hull collision/waterline.
- **F1:** complete both-compact-berths/blocked-exit/dry-Spindle/surface launch observations.
- **F2:** clear slots, reach supported dock, configure medium and capture/launch with full physical clearance through actual controls.
- **F3:** complete prepared/lock save/reload, interruption/focus, changed obstruction, exactly-once and incapacity fallback observations.

Physical recovery, final-route legacy clearance, full visuals/captions/audio, human duration/enjoyment and representative GPU evidence remain open. No full expedition/recovery/browser matrix or M1 acceptance is claimed.

Root must inspect this source, reconcile the proposed contracts/compatibility and commit the new shared baseline before specialists start. Visual work should consume `CARRIER_LAYOUT`/`carrierStructure` and preserve walking clearance; presentation should use explicit sound origins and keep saved provenance exact. Main retains shared simulation/registry/world/save/runtime composition ownership. Fresh non-author Astra xhigh and Sol 6.1 max review plus coordinator inspection remain required for batch acceptance, with a separate integrated M1 gate.
